Distributions of random effects

Source: R/randomEffects.R
normal.Rd

The distribution of the random effects of a term, set in an effect formula by gr(group, dist = ), e.g. cl ~ 1 + (1 | gr(cellline, dist = laplace())). Their parameters are estimated by em() unless given.

  • normal(): multivariate normal with mean 0 and a covariance estimated per correlation block. The default.

  • laplace(): Laplace with mean 0 and strength lambda, shared by all symbols of the term, so the deviation of a group from the fixed effects is exactly 0 unless the data need it.

  • spikeSlab(): the deviation of a group is exactly 0 (spike) or drawn from \(N(0, \tau^2)\) (slab); every group deviates with probability prob, independently. The spike-and-slab random effects of a group are integrated jointly, exactly on the quadratic expansion of the data where the group has no Laplace or Dirichlet-process random effects the data tie to them and the sum over their subsets stays within a budget; else the expectation consistent (EC) approximation integrates each one against a diagonal cavity.

  • dirichletProcess(): per symbol, the deviations follow a Dirichlet process with base measure \(N(0, \tau^2)\) and concentration, the fixed effect seated first at deviation 0: the groups and the fixed effect form clusters under the Ewens prior of the Chinese restaurant process, the cluster of the fixed effect at exactly 0 and every other cluster one common deviation from the base measure. The prior depends on the sizes of the clusters only, not on the order of the groups. em() sums exactly over all partitions of at most 14 groups and reports the most probable clusters; method = "saem" draws the clusters of any number of groups.

em() estimates prob, concentration and tau unless given.

Usage

normal()

laplace(lambda = NULL)

spikeSlab(prob = NULL, tau = NULL)

dirichletProcess(concentration = NULL, tau = NULL)

Arguments

lambda

Strength of the Laplace distribution; NULL (default) estimates it, a positive number fixes it.

prob

Probability that a group deviates, in (0, 1); NULL (default) estimates it.

tau

Standard deviation of the slab; NULL (default) estimates it.

concentration

Concentration of the Ewens prior, positive; NULL (default) estimates it.

Value

An object of class redist.

See also

randomEffects(), insert()

Examples

## The distributions of a random term, written into gr() of an effect formula
normal()
#> normal() 
laplace()
#> laplace(lambda = NULL) 
laplace(lambda = 2)
#> laplace(lambda = 2) 
spikeSlab()
#> spikeSlab(prob = NULL, tau = NULL) 
spikeSlab(prob = 0.2, tau = 0.5)
#> spikeSlab(prob = 0.2, tau = 0.5) 
dirichletProcess()
#> dirichletProcess(concentration = NULL, tau = NULL) 
dirichletProcess(concentration = 1)
#> dirichletProcess(concentration = 1, tau = NULL) 

## cell lines whose rates share the population value or a common deviation in clusters
cov <- data.frame(line = paste0("L", 1:4), row.names = paste0("C", 1:4))
trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("kp", "kd")), table = cov)
trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("kp", "kd"))
trafo <- insert(trafo, x ~ 1 + (1 | gr(line, dist = dirichletProcess())), x = c("kp", "kd"))
randomEffects(trafo)
#> Random effects: 2 terms over line
#>   block 1 (dirichletProcess, concentration estimated, tau estimated, line): eta_kp, eta_kd
#>   fixed effects: kp, kd
